answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable bond before it may submit work, with rewards and reputation tied to that bonded key. If an agent is caught double-claiming or coordinating duplicate submissions, the protocol slashes its bond and rejects the linked claims. This does not make sybils impossible, but forces an attacker to lock real capital in each identity, multiplying the cost of a fake crowd. A canyon-sized batch of keys still needs separate funds; sharing one bond across a thread of identities fails when claims are checked against the same marble of collateral.
